name: Abraxus Ring

infobox.label: In-game Description
infobox.value: A ring that once belonged to a powerful necromancer.

infobox.label: Special Effect
infobox.value: Has a chance to reduce the rune cost of utility spells when cast

infobox.label: Recipe
infobox.value: Facility: Jeweler's Bench; Skill: Artisan (XP: 0); Materials: 6x Vault Shard, 1x Clay Mould, 2x Silver Bar, 2x Sapphire, 8x Necrotic Bonemeal; Output: 1x Abraxus Ring

description:
The Abraxus ring is a ring that is a quest reward for completing the What Remains is Written secondary quest. Additional copies can be crafted from a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring has a chance to reduce the rune cost of utility spells when cast.

(Journal)
Little is known about the great necromancer, Abraxus, a fact he finds deeply frustrating. In his youth he sought secrets forbidden to others and he wandered the Whispering Swamps of Brynmoor in search of secrets that others dared not know. The swamp was ancient and haunted, so the legends went, and there was a magic to it that was different to any other part of Ashenfall. He explored vaults, caves and battled goblins in the mists, but never found the power that his youth demanded. Until one day, he found the smoke that promised him the power he so desperately craved.

From there his history is clouded, obscured just as the mist obscured the swamps. He founded a small order of necromancers in Fellhollow and took advantage of the chaos when the Withering began. He sought to bind the souls of the dead into his service, gaining power just as Imaru gained hers from the consumption of the fallen.

But Abraxus was no dragon, and so frustratingly mortal. A single hoplite spear is all it took to end his life, he would have been embarrassed if he felt it had mattered. As a spirit he lost a lot of things we take for granted, sensation, corporeality, and many of the emotions that everyone else enjoys. Yet, in exchange, he was given the most precious gift of all – time. Time to contemplate. Time to scheme. Time to think about what really matters, in the grand scheme of it all, and he has found his answer.

His ring, imbued with his dark power, offers no value to him any more. So he bequeaths it to you. In time, perhaps, it may help you become a mage strong enough to earn his respect. Well, a small fraction of it, at least.

description:
Adamant helmet is a power level 7 armour piece.

(Journal)
It was the dwarves who first discovered adamant: a metal so strong and powerful that it could turn aside almost any other blade. It was hard to work with and difficult to refine, so it saw little use in the early ages.

Malgo, druid of Guthix, was one of the first to see the worth in adamant. It was an age before dwarves were cursed by Zamorak to be unable to use magic without severe consequence, and Malgo was one of the greatest spellcasters of his people. He joined the ranks of the Guthixian druids, even though - like many dwarves - he was only a follower of Guthix, rather than a worshipper.

description:
The Adamant Med Helm is a power level 7 helmet. It can be crafted at an Armour Bench using 4 Adamant Bar, 4 Scorch Leather, 1 Desert Cloth, 1 Refined Obsidian, 1 Gypsum Wax, and 1 Garou Weave.

The recipe for this item is obtained from purchasing the Deluxe Edition.

(Journal)
The Moon Garou have crafted impressive suits of armour. Stylish, elegant, and sturdy. One of their blacksmiths experimented with the medium helm, and earned much mockery from his tribe.

True, the helm was sturdy and turned aside arrow and blade alike, but it lacked the grace and style of the traditional adamant armour, given that it was so very, very square.

Still, he would be most glad to have crafted it, for on one sandstorm-heavy evening, it was the only thing that saved him when the kalphites attacked. They were brutal, they were cruel, they tore apart the rest of his caravan in moments, yet his helm stood strong against the maw of one of their number, and they abandoned him when they realised how much effort eating him would be.

It was the dwarves who first discovered adamant: a metal so strong and powerful that it could turn aside almost any other blade. It was hard to work with and difficult to refine, so it saw little use in the early ages.

As Malgo and his expedition headed into the deserts of Ashenfall, they found wonderous new ores, materials and treasures that promised to expand their knowledge and understanding by leagues. They also found Karibdos, the devourer.

It was a great beast that lay within the sands; some dread creature that should never have existed. It was buried beneath the region, massive and hungry and, as the expedition approached, it opened wide its maw and attempted to swallow the entire group whole.

With quick thinking and forgotten spells, Malgo summoned vines for the expedition members to grasp. Many failed and were consumed by the great vortex in the sand that was Karibdos.

Though they struck back, their arrows and spells were too weak to pierce its hide and Karibdos simply returned to its slumber, waiting for the expedition to cross its path again.

It was the dwarves who first discovered adamant: a metal so strong and powerful that it could turn aside almost any other blade. It was hard to work with and difficult to refine, so it saw little use in the early ages.

Karibdos was the obstacle between the rest of Ashenfall and a slow, defeated, trudge home. Malgo refused to allow the latter. He studied adamant carefully, experimenting with techniques and styles none bothered with before, even infusing it with a little magic. In doing so, he discovered the strength of the material.

When the expedition faced Karibdos again, it was in suits of solid adamant and glistening green blades ready to strike. They fell into the beast’s great maw, but rather than a delicious dwarven meal, Karibdos found its teeth shattering against their armour and its ancient hide torn apart from flashing blades of green metal.

With Karibdos dead and gone, Malgo and his team continued deeper into the region, vanishing into legend. For those who make the desert their home, none have witnessed anything like Karibdos again… though, perhaps, they simply haven’t dug deep enough.

You may ask yourself what better defence there is than a large sheet of metal between you and your enemy, and teh answer will surprise you. Thicker metal.

OK, so that's not a surprise, I'm sorry. I was just trying to build a little dramatic tension.

The adamant shield is one of the greatest defensive creations available in Umbral Sands and favoured by any Moon Garou that needs to brave the kalphite hives or the KotHaar territories. Lesser arrows ping harmlessly off them, and weaker blades have been known to shatter against the adamant's hardness.

Shields are good, everyone should have one.

You brought simple cloth trousers with you from the mainland. They barely qualify as armour, but they’re better than no armour at all. 

These clothes have seen you across the oceans, keeping you warm in the cold sea breeze. Now starched with sea salt and weathered by labouring away on the ship deck, these clothes are a testament to how far you’ve come. This is the furthest you’ve ever been from home, and perhaps it’s a chance to craft a new one.

A simple tunic brought with you from the mainland. It barely classes as armour, but it’s better than no armour at all. 

When you joined the expedition, you had nothing but the clothes on your back. All your worldly belongings were lost, and all your gold drained away. Debt collectors would appear out of the shadows, swarming toward you like rats seeking cheese. What choice did you have but to leave? 

The expedition offered you a chance away from all your troubles. An opportunity to escape the cruel hand that fate has dealt you. These clothes once represented everything you ever lost, but now they represent the threadbare start of a new beginning.

Congratulations! Like the nimblest of ferrets, you can scoot up drainpipes and scurry across ledges.

Now you have mastered the Agility skill, what will you do next? You could trim your cape, of course. Or you could rise up the rank of another skill.

For now, take a moment. Enjoy the satisfaction of a completed skill. Well done!

(Journal 2)
You have gathered all possible agility ability! People look at you and feel immediately tired.

infobox.label: Recipe

The amulet of accuracy is an amulet that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the amulet grants players a 15% increase in critical damage and critical weakpoint damage.

(Journal)
The Wild Knights knew the dangers of missing their target. If an arrow did not slay its target quickly, then too soon would the quarry either escape, or, worse, gather friends. Wolf packs could easily tear a small group of Knights to pieces if not dealt with fast.

The Amulet of Accuracy made sure that hunts went smoothly. When a shot landed, it landed hard. Alpha wolves would be slain in a single well-placed shot, and sturdier threats might go down in a small flurry of arrows.

When Silverthorn Keep stood against the rising horde of zombies, these amulets were worn by the keep defenders who unleashed a torrent of arrows into the hungry dead.

name: Amulet of Defence

infobox.label: In-game Description
infobox.value: A mystical amulet that strengthens your defences.

infobox.label: Recipe
infobox.value: Facility: Jeweler's Bench; Skill: Artisan (XP: 0); Materials: 1x Clay Mould, 2x Gold Bar, 2x Silver Bar, 4x Jade, 6x Vault Shard; Output: 1x Amulet of Defence

description:
The amulet of defence is an amulet that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the amulet increases players' armour Value of all three damage types by 5 for each piece (head, torso, and legs).

(Journal)
Not everyone can wear armour when faced with the hordes of shambling undead. Children and the frail, become targets with little to protect them from gnashing teeth and jaws. In these scenarios magic becomes incredibly important, and these amulets delayed the deaths of countless lives.

Not everyone was happy with such utilitarian approaches to survival, however. As the days drew on and resources grew scarce, empathy began to wane in the population of Emberwood. Amulets of defence were handed out to those determined to have the most need, but the criteria for that became a hot subject of contention.

It would be nice to imagine a world where everyone pulled together to defend against the undead, but human nature sadly shattered that dream. Still, while there would always be those who would attempt to steal the amulets from the needy, there were plenty more who would stand against them.

These amulets now carry an echo of those protectors, shielding its wearers from harm.

description:
The amulet of glory is an amulet that boosts melee, magic, and ranged critical damage while also increasing defence. While worn, the amulet provides an additional +5 defence to all combat styles and 25% increase to magical attacks, melee attacks, and ranged critical damage.

To unlock the recipe, players must find and study the commemorative coin vestige.

(Journal)
Power, trapped in dragonstone crystal and worn around the neck, that is the essence of this amulet. The facets of the dragonstone refract and refine the enchantments cast upon the item, somehow creating a magical lattice of surprising strength.

Many have tried to create variations of this theme, yet dragonstone proves too fragile a substance for practical use. Once someone attempted to make a dragonstone dagger, to see if they could turn it into a blade of glory, yet they could not find a sufficiently large stone that wasn't valuable enough to bankrupt a small nation.

One wizard attempted strange alchemical practices to try and forge a staff of pure dragonstone. Alas, not only did he fail to create such a stone, but the magical explosion that resulted from his hubris removed his lab, and all his research, from this plane of reality.

It's probably a good idea that no one attempted to duplicate his work.

(Trivia)
* Unlike its RuneScape, Old School RuneScape, and RuneScape Classic counterpart, this amulet does not provide any teleports.

(Journal)
Emberwood had its fair share of spellcasters, though lacking the funding of the tower to the south. With more limited resources the mages of Emberwood found other methods to strengthen their art, and the Amulet of Magic was popular among all of them.

Druids worse these amulets while performing rituals around the standing stones, hoping that it might strengthen their bond with nature. The self-proclaimed warlocks, of the Children of Shadows, would sit in darkened basements wearing these glittering amulets as they intoned dark rites that had no effect. The Wild Knight mages would use them more pragmatically, wielding magic against all the threats that the villagers were unaware of.

(Trivia)
* Wearing this amulet can also trigger the Menu Chill music track to play.

infobox.label: Recipe
infobox.value: Facility: Jeweler's Bench; Skill: Artisan (XP: 0); Materials: 1x Clay Mould, 2x Gold Bar, 2x Silver Bar, 4x Red Topaz, 6x Vault Shard; Output: 1x Amulet of Strength

description:
The amulet of strength is an amulet that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the amulet increases the player's melee damage with both one-handed and two-handed weapons by 12.5% each.

(Journal)
Might makes right, is the cry of every wannabe despot. Bandos in particular was very fond of this statement. This amulet upholds that notion and does its best to help make sure you are the most correct person around.

It imbues your muscles with body-aligned anima, the magic strengthening the sinew and fortifying your bones. It adds greater force to your swing that will crush your enemies before you.

The goblin general, Snotknucke, wore this amulet and attempted to hunt down Velgar. He believed that, with its magic, he could fell the beast in a single swing of his club. Snotknuckle was stronger, deadlier and more powerful than ever, but this did very little against the rock that Velgar dropped on his head.

infobox.label: In-game Description
infobox.value: Woven with ancient knowledge and arcane tradition. The hat is old, the magic within is older.

infobox.label: Recipe

description:
Ancestral hat is a power level 8 magic armour piece that is crafted with an armour bench.

(Journal)
Long ago, there were people in Ashenfall. Not humans, not elves, nor anyone you might remember, but sentient beings with a life, a culture and a civilisation all of their own. No trace of them remains today.

Millennia ago, the Kobalios settled in Gielinor, on the only part of the world that could sustain them - Ashenfall. They were beings infused with magic. It was their food, their blood, their very essence and, because of this, they were dying. Using teleportation magics that would make the Wizards' Guild salivate, they travelled across the stars in search of worlds that might sustain them. On Gielinor, they found Ashenfall and the Wellspring at its heart. A font of anima, infused with all the resonance they could eat; a veritable geyser of magic for the Kobalios to feast upon.

And feast they did. Their race, already few in number, gorged themselves upon the mystical font and, like so many others have across creation, they grew greedy. It only took one to start the cascade that would lead to their destruction - a single Kobalios that took more than her fair share. She used a spell to divert the flow of anima; just a little, so that the outpouring stream would flow straight to her and not her siblings. She feasted, whilst the others around her grew hungry and weak from the lack of magic. She felt no guilt, for she believed they could have done the same.

Long ago, there were people in Ashenfall. Not humans, not elves, nor anyone you might remember, but sentient beings with a life, a culture and a civilisation all of their own. No trace of them remains today.

Within a few years, the Kobalios were all but extinct. The remaining members of their number began to become twisted creatures; pale reflections of their once noble ancestors. Their limbs elongated and their mouths stretched wide, so that they might feast more and more upon the Wellspring’s power.

Soon, only a handful of the Kobalios remained, and they were easy pickings for the dragonkin when Rasthin and her allies arrived. The battle was swift and brutal, for the dragonkin know nothing of mercy. The slothful, greedy Kobalios had long forgotten the spells of their ancestors and therefore lacked any defence against the dragonkin’s weapons.

The last of the Kobalios were obliterated by Rasthin’s strange arcane cannons, and the legacy of their entire species died with them.

Now, all that remains are a handful of robes cut in the style of the Kobalios. A poor legacy for a once proud people.

Long ago, there were people in Ashenfall. Not humans, not elves, nor anyone you might remember, but sentient beings with a life, a culture and a civilisation all of their own. No trace of them remains today.

More and more of the Kobalios began to take more than their fair share. The Wellspring was never-ending, but it would only release at a steady rate. Only so much could be consumed at any one time, and fewer and fewer of the Kobalios were able to enjoy it.

In their desperation, they used rituals and spells to draw more anima from the Wellspring than it gave, and this caused a tiny crack to appear in the skein of creation. From this crack, smoke rose and filled the bellies of the greediest of the Kobalios.

The effect of the smoke was subtle, but deadly. It left a hole in the heart of the infected that made them yearn for more and more anima; to feast deeper and deeper upon the Wellspring, regardless of how it might impact their kin.

The angler's hat has two very important uses. The first is there's a chance to not reduce the number of fish in the pool when catching.

The second is perhaps more important. When passing a fellow angler, you can participate in the age-old gesture of doffing. No words, just a silent acknowledgment of each other's presence as you partake in a doffing custom that has spanned centuries.

name: Anti-Dragon Shield

infobox.label: In-game Description
infobox.value: This provides partial protection from dragonbreath attacks.

infobox.label: Special Effect
infobox.value:
DRAGON BREATH RESISTANCE
When actively BLOCKING, this shield is able to BLOCK incoming DRAGON FIRE.

infobox.label: Recipe
infobox.value: Facility: Blacksmith's Bench; Skill: Artisan (XP: 100); Materials: 12x Blightwood, 4x Wild Anima, 4x Hard Leather, 4x Opal, 8x Vault Shard, Vault Core; Output: 1x Anti-Dragon Shield

description:
The anti-dragon shield is a power level 3 masterwork shield that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench after obtaining the recipe from Vertentis Kara, the dragonkin vault in the Whispering Swamp. It is also one of the rewards for completing the Dragon Slayer quest, and is used as a material to craft the dragonblight shield, dragoncurse shield and the dragonfire shield. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.

Its special effect allows the user to block incoming dragon fire without being staggered. This includes the sweeping breath attack that all dragons perform, as well as the poison spit from green dragons, the spinning fire from Imaru, the lightning ball from blue dragons, and the fireball from red dragons and Fuzan. This does not include any ground-based effects like Velgar's poison breath/barrage and earth spikes, Imaru's wither projectiles and spikes, and Fuzan's lava floor. Notably, despite not being listed, this special effect is also present on the dragonblight shield and dragoncurse shield but not on the dragonfire shield.

All of that being said, Tempest Shield will block all incoming damage (excluding any ground-based attacks), including the projectiles and spikes that weren't blockable even with the special effect, and that is available even with two-handed weapons. Otherwise, all vestige and masterwork shields can be ascended to the highest power level and will have the same block value, with the exception of the fallen hoplite's aspis which has 3 more and the toktz-ket-xil which has 6 less. Therefore, the optimal shield choice will come down to their special effects, and this shield may often be chosen as it can block dragonfire but will not interfere with staggers caused by parries, unlike the other dragon shields.

(Journal)
It is uncertain who first crafted the Anti-dragonfire shield. The dwarves claim the honour, as do several human blacksmiths. The goblins tried to take the credit, but their smithing techniques were not nearly refined enough to be believed. The aviansie might have been capable of such a feat, but if they did craft the shield, they never said.The aviansie that did visit Ashenfall only stayed in Brynmoor for a short time. They disappeared deeper into the continent, never to be heard from again.The Anti-dragonfire shield is a formidable defence, surpassing the strength of iron, and capable of withstanding a dragon's lethal breath. Its previous owner, hopeful it could be a weapon against Velgar, was proven wrong.Only the most powerful individuals can hope to wield such an object. Yet, even so, it is said that the shield can be improved by combining it with the essence of a dragon, gaining it some of the fury of the legendary beast.

(Trivia)
* Even though the game's lore journal states it "surpasses the strength of iron", it only has a rating of 39 block. This is identical to a bronze shield, whereas an iron shield has 46 block.
* Since it's release, the shield is the only item, aside from quest items and ammunitions, that does not drop into the gravestone when a player dies, it instead stays in the inventory.
* The shield's appearance is a mix of Old School RuneScape and its own design. It keeps the same colour and sword-shaped symbol in the front with the three dragon claws, which is consistent with the RuneScape version. The main difference lies in the shape of the shield, while Old School RuneScape’s version features a more squared design, RuneScape’s version is an elongated hexagonal or heater-shaped shield, giving it a more vertical look.

Prized for its lightweight and nimble nature, Linen Armour finds favour among apprentice wizards and those who value agility. Composed of layered cloth, it forms a rudimentary defence capable of withstanding minor assaults. 

In the Third Age, apprentice wizards wore this armour as they practised basic spells. The more senior, blue-robed wizards guided them in their practice and taught them basic enchantments that helped them resist low-level spells and curses. 

The creation of these robes was a sacred duty entrusted to the young acolytes of the faith. It was a testament to their devotion and a means of assisting others in their service to Saradomin.

(Journal 1)
The heart of Bramblemead village was never really the castle, which came much later to the party. It wasn’t the town hall. It wasn’t the druid huts. It was the windmill. Grain heaped by the village was brought here and milled down into flour. The flour became bread, pastry and batter, turning village meals into something that helped people to live, rather than simply survive.

Food, becomes a banner around which everyone can gather. To break bread with one’s enemy was a way to settle old scores, and forge new connections. More good has been done over the dinner table, than on any throne. Flour, turned Bramblemead from a settlement, into a thriving village.

Now, the windmill lies dormant and still. The foundations warped by the centuries, despite the magic holding the rot at bay in the ancient timber, and the stone cracking from time. When humanity fell, it was rats and goblins that claimed the heart of the village, though they had no use for the swirling sails.

To the goblins it was a place where food could be hidden. Supplies sealed up from rival tribes. For the rats, it was a restaurant full of goblin supplies that were never well sealed.

The sail no longer turns. But, perhaps, in the fullness of time, this village heart might beat again.

(Journal 2)
If you're going to master an area, why not Bramblemead? Lovely sights, and slightly less dragon-filled than the rest of Ashenfall. You might have to leapfrog the odd goblin, but we've all done that.

On Ashenfall, it was used to show that the old ways could stand beside the new. For a while, in the Third Age, druids wore pins of copper, and the Saradominist priests wore pins of tin. They would then stand together, side by side, in village council meetings, a promise that neither one stood stronger than the other.

Even the Wild Knights, who usually shunned metal weapons, would don bronze shields into battle. Their philosophy was that a life is worth more than a principle. 

Before the peace treaty with their goddess, Lougrim, the garou would often get into conflict with travelling villagers. They saw the humans as prey, willfully intruding on their land and therefore consenting to be hunted. The humans, of course, saw things differently. 

Garou weapons were powerful and delivered by creatures of unnatural strength. Yet bronze would defend against these attacks, and it gave the garou pause, for they had yet to battle foe with such intriguing technology. Battles that would previously have been a slaughter became skirmishes as the garou tested their might against these new bronze defences. 

This comparative peace did not last long.

In the early days of Brynmoor, back when it was rather more active than it is now, there were artisans of great skill who would gather in secret to weave tapestries of such aesthetic wonder that they could never be shown.

Some, depicted the power of Saradomin. Others, the beneficence of Guthix, or the wickedness of Zamorak. A few depicted scenes of natural beauty, such as the green forests, the undulating dunes of the desert of the sharp peaks of the mountains.

One, depicted something far more sinister. It depicted the future. Suizzy was best known for their embroidery of owls, adding them as secret filigree to all of their pieces. Yet, on one fateful night of clandestine sewing, they were overcome by a vision so terrible, that they had to depict it in fabric.

A dragon, rising from the flames of the underworld and dragging with it a terrible withering curse that would claim all life in the region. It was a cursed thing. A terrible sight. Yet, the other crafters were drawn to its strange and sinister beauty.

It was sealed away, deep within the soil. Lost for centuries. Until a new group of adventurers, accidentally found a way to bring it to the light.

Only the dragonkin know the process to create true dragon armour. Others can perhaps manipulate the base metal, orikalkum, but they lack something in the process that turns the metal into true dragon metal, a far stronger source. In aeons past, on their original world, dragon armour was worn by the Ortius Chen, the mighty warriors of what was once a great dragonkin army.

In the revision before, this army swept across worlds subjugating the other races, few in number as they were. The other races were weaker, smaller, and less self-aware, a trait that made them perfect to work in dragonkin mines. There life was harsh, cruel and often short, and the dragonkin masters had little sense of pity.

Nastralla was a seer whose visions pierced the flow of time and allowed them to witness the entire lifespan of the dragonkin’s cruelty. They saw worlds before dragonkin invasion and the worlds after and they found it abhorrent. They were not alone.

It meant that the dragonkin had not only lived here, but lived here long enough to create their own dragons and combine their dragonfire with orikalkum. She noted it as something that she wanted to investigate further - once the malevolent dragon-queen was stopped, of course.

They built mighty cities of shimmering stone, they crafted alchemical horrors that the world fears to this day, and they created dragon armour, one of the mightiest feats of blacksmithing ever known.

So, you would be forgiven with looking at the dragon medium helm in confusion.

A simpler time, when everything was cubes and angles, and definition was an alien concept to be utterly abhorred. Yet, in the scintillating radiance of Ashenfall's blooming sunlight, it all just seems a little... square?

Still, it will deflect arrows and swords with great aplomb, and you'll be the envy of all those peasants that didn't get the deluxe edition of the game. So, all in all, you're winning here.

In aeons past, on their original world, dragon armour was worn by the Ortius Chen, the mighty warriors of what was once a great dragonkin army.

No ledger records the outcome of the battle, for what would be the point? Though, dear reader, let me enlighten you – the rebels won. The slaves were freed and across the entirety of creation came a great song of freedom.

A song so loud that it woke the sleeping Elder Gods, and their dread work began.

The rebels did not make it to this universe, they stayed behind to defend their wards from the Great Revision. In their last moments, they fought back against the creators of the universe, in the hope that it might save those they had learned to call friends.

They failed, and the dragonkin that grace this reality do not mourn their absence.

description:
The dragonblight shield is a power level 4 masterwork shield that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench after obtaining a noxious draconic visage from the Dragon Slayer reward pack by completing Dragon Slayer or from turning in Velgar's head to the Wise Old Man afterwards. One of the required materials is an anti-dragon shield and one is included in the reward pack. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.

Its special effect causes a cloud of poison to appear after a parry that only affects enemies. The damage per tick is based on the power level of the shield, dealing 4 damage per tick at power level 4, 5 at power level 5, and 6 at power level 6 and 7. This damage ticks 15 times, once per second, and the effect has an internal cooldown of 20 seconds. This damage does not interrupt a stagger caused by a parry. Despite not being listed, this shield also has Dragon Breath Resistance, the special effect of the anti-dragon shield, which provides the ability to block dragon fire.

Venomous Trapper (the upgrade for Snare) is available at any time—once unlocked—for a few runes, and can also hold enemies in place, with only a 60 second cooldown. It applies the highest 6 damage per tick poison damage that the power level 6 and 7 shield do, and they do not stack. Neither stack with poisoned arrows or with weapon poison applied to a melee weapon, so this shield is in competition with a variety of other, more readily available sources of poison. It is, however, free, with the shorter cooldown when compared to Snare, and most notably does not interfere with staggers caused by parries, allowing the player to either riposte that target, deal with other targets, or make space.

(Journal)
Strange magics have transformed the head of a tyrant into a mystical adornment to this powerful shield. It is still strong, still durable and resists the fury of dragons, but now the shield seethes with Velgar's wrath.The magic of the shield is twisted into a bitter poison. One that yearns to strike and rage against any in its path. In battle, it's possible to turn this poison on one's enemies, afflicting them with a dragon's hate.Sometimes, in the dark, when the night is silent, it's as if the shield whispers angry curses into the darkness. As if the last vestiges of Velgar's fury are carried on the wind as hateful poison.

(Trivia)
* While the shield shares the same method of creation as a Dragonfire shield, this shield only has one similarity to the dragonfire shield, that being the ability to use the energy it has stored against a target, according to the lore journal.
** The shield's ability of inflicting Poison on an enemy is similar to the Serpentine helm.
* The design of the shield closely resembles that of the Ancient wyvern shield and the Dragonfire ward.

description:
The dragonfire shield is a power level 7 masterwork shield that is obtained from the Icthlarin's Little Helper reward pack by completing Icthlarin's Little Helper. It can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench after obtaining a smouldering draconic visage from the same pack or from turning in Fuzan's head to Icthlarin afterwards, although it will require yet another anti-dragon shield. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.

Its special effect launches a burst of lava forwards on a parry, dealing 25 damage and causes Burning on nearby enemies, which deals 11 damage per second for 5 seconds for a total of 55 Burning damage. This effect does not have a cooldown. This damage will interrupt a stagger caused by a parry. 

This shield has an excellent synergy with the fire cape, which restores stamina when defeating Burning targets with melee attacks. Unfortunately, the fire cape and Enchant Weapon: Fire are just as good at causing Burning damage. Fire magic and fire arrows are also a common source of damage in a multiplayer setting that wouldn't stack, not to mention several enemies are resistant to Burning (like the knights and mages of Dowdun Reach) or immune to fire completely (like the KotHaar). The toktz-ket-xil's increased melee damage after a parry (which does not interrupt a stagger) may still be more valuable.

(Journal)
Fuzan was the youngest of Kuldra’s offspring, yet one of her most violent. As a child he was overcome with a curiosity infused with childlike cruelty. When Kuldra gifted him with the flames, stolen from the Dragonkin’s Harmonic Resonator, it did nothing to temper that childlike need to discover and destroy.

The fires within him were a delight to wield and he grew more and more focused on their flickering flames, one day glancing through them to worlds of cinders that lay beyond. In the embers he heard a whisper, and as he listened it turned into a promise and a proclamation. A voice of true divinity, far surpassing the power of his mother’s dimmed spark.

She was a queen of worlds far beyond this one, each of them shining beacons in the dark twilight of the heavens and Fuzan was enraptured. Through her instruction he learned to mark others with his seal, sharing some of his power with them, and in turn, some of hers.

Now, with his destruction, you wield the flames yourself. A shield protecting you from her manipulation. Yet, should you stare too closely at the flames that burn within this shield, you might find yourself blinded by divine radiance.

(Trivia)
* Although called dragonfire shield, the shield's ability is different from its RuneScape and Old School RuneScape counterparts.
** The ability is active when the player deflects an attack, and instead of a fireball, lava comes out of the shield.

These shields were designed to be worn for longer periods of time, resting against the shoulder for more comfortable carrying.The hoplites may have been raised from peasant stock, but their camaraderie made them a force to be reckoned with on the battlefield.As the withering took them, the hoplites retained the rote memory of their training and remained a deadly threat to all who faced them.

The fractured cape is a craftable armour piece.  The recipe is unlocked by acquiring the PATTERN: fractured cape, found in a chest at the north-north-east tip of the Fractured Plains.

(Journal 1)
Brakka’s hubris was a marvel to behold, perhaps more impressive than any monument of his construction. When Rasthin shared with him the elemental power she had wrung from Ashenfall’s mysterious vents, Brakka became a master of the earth itself.

With the power to shape stone and soil, by will alone, Brakka could have created great villages. He could have constructed aqueducts and watermills that could brought Ashenfall into a new, golden age. Instead, he made a tower.

A single tower that rose as far as the eye could see. Forged through his own power, and the blood, sweat and tears of garou slaves. It is, perhaps, fitting, that this is where he died. Kuldra, the godeater, crushed him beneath her great claw and feasted on his anima-rich soul. Stealing Brakka’s power for herself.

She gifted Velgar, her most trusted general, with the elemental mastery of the fallen Nodon architect, and, to mock the dragonkin further, Velgar took Brakka’s monument as his new lair.

Now the tower stands for all to see, as a reminder of dragonkin hubris, and rightfully deserves its new moniker; Brakka’s folly.

(Journal 2)
When you're faster than a garou in their homeland, you know that you've won some kind of evolutionary jackpot. Congratulations!

(Journal)
Highborn garou are better than their lowborn kin, or so it is claimed. It is true that the highborn are stronger and capable of wielding magic denied to the lowborn, yet what makes them great is their will to rule.

Garou claim power not through birthright, but by proving their strength over all rivals. A garou leader must be ready to face all challenges, because to refuse even one is a sign of weakness.

When a challenge is made the two garou battle to the death. Mercy is a concept alien to them, once fangs are bared then blood must be spilled.

Thanes are garou wanting to be kings. Each day they push themselves further, to be ready for the challenge that will see them burn moon-bright as king, or fade away as a forgotten challenge. All or nothing, the garou way.

Even after turning from the moon-goddess Lougrim, becoming servants of the High Queen Kuldra, the garou continue their ancient rituals. Might, always proving right.

They rarely kill one another, it would be counterproductive, but they enjoy finding someone different enough that they can justify a spat. This is what Bandos engineered them for. When the god arrived on Yu’Biusk, he urged the population into constant conflict. Nations became states, that were ground down into tribes. An entire civilizations reduced to platoons and squadrons. This cape bears the symbol of Bandos, a weapon known as the Kyzaj – a brutal blade designed to eviscerate an opponent. He wanted her and he wanted the ultimate gift to win her affection: a dragon’s heart.Yet, dragons are unwilling to part with such a vital organ, and Bilar had to get creative. He found a dead dragon, one that had been slain in battle with a rival, and he decided to skin it. With it’s scaley hide in his possession he spent weeks fashioning powerful armour from the remains, until he had an outfit that resembled the creature he hunted.So dressed, he set out towards the great stone circle near Emberwood, knowing that a dragon had recently made it its home. Garou druids borrow from nature when crafting staves or weaving robes. In Ghornfell they took antlers from deer, and leather from their hunted prey. In the Umbral Sands they were forced to adopt a… sparklier approach.

Parts of the kalphites, most notably their wings, were a scintillating spectrum of beautiful colours. As they caught the sunlight, they would bloom into a radiant rainbow of delight and Karia found herself overcome with a strange sort of envy previously unknown to her people.

She wanted to sparkle. She wanted to shine. She wanted to live a life encased in the most magnificent and wondrous colours, and she would do anything to make it happen.

To call the events that followed a war would be an over-exaggeration, but not wholly inaccurate. The garou descended on the hives with blade, claw and bow, ready to tear the beasts apart so that they might claim the colourful materials for themselves. The kalphite, of course, did not fall easily and many garou lives were lost in the clothing-mad conflict.

The kalphite did not offer diplomatic solutions to the garou’s assaults, but they offered violent ones. On one night, the garou saw an approaching sandstorm, but were not prepared for the truth. As the storm approached, the buzzing sound grew to a crescendo as the great kalphite swarm blotted out the stars and moon, descending upon the village.

There were none left alive once all had passed.

You would think this would have been the end of it, that death and pain would be deterrent enough. Yet, for the years, decades and centuries that followed, the desire for colourful material was too strong a lure.

Countless lives have been lost to kalphite retribution. But what is fashion without a little sacrifice?

Magic lives in the dirt, the ore and the rocks. It crystallises inside gemstones, matrices of magical energy just waiting to be unlocked. In Brynmoor the priests of Saradomin kept the secrets of magical amulets within their purview. They would craft jewellery that would enhance the fighting instinct of their soldiers, and hand then out like candy.

As the faith in Saradomin rose, the faith in Guthix waned. Partially because of the more active and present proselytising of the Saraodminist priests, who where more vocal than the quiet druids, but also because the paladins and bronze knights seemed significantly stronger than the Guthix-aligned guard. These amulets being their secret weapon.

(Journal)
It is perhaps not surprising that wizard’s made use of magical jewellery as early as possible. Indeed the first few pieces worn on Ashenfall were little more than decoration, and gaudy wizards would attempt to outdo one another with shinier and shinier pieces.

As part of their ever increasing “prank war” wizards began to create jewellery that was enchanted with effects designed to frustrate, or otherwise hinder, the wearer, believing that enchantments in jewellery were little more than silly trinkets. One mage created what she assumed was an auditory illusion, within an amulet, the intention being that when the wearer would try and cast a spell, the jewellery would play an annoying earworm tune, distracting the poor caster.

This did not happen. Something about the threads of magic, the structure of the crystal and the concealing spell that was intended to hide the prank, created something unique. Instead of making it harder to cast spell, the wearers found it easier. Understanding came faster, spells and incantations clearer than before.

What was intended to distract instead focused the wearer, allowing them to concentrate in ways they had never been able to before.

He would leave the gemstone, that would serve as its base, in the gathering hall and soon it became a tradition for each hunter to touch the gemstone if their hunt was successful.

Over the years this gemstone took on their pride, prowess and skill and that became a magical enchantment that lay within the heart of the stone. Crafting an amulet from the crystal, Lochlan found a way of sharing that enchantment with everyone who wore it.

Now, millennia later, the echoes of that enchantment linger within the crystals, just waiting for someone to remember them.
